sections.title: Setting
sections.text: Lviv sits at about 283 m above sea level, in a basin that runs from about 128 m to 476 m. It lies in the Central European mixed forests ecoregion.

sections.title: Climate
sections.text: Across the surrounding basin of about 16,336 km², rainfall averages about 588 mm a year, moderately seasonal, with July the wettest month. Temperatures there average 7.5 °C, from -4.5 °C in January to 18.1 °C in July. Its aridity index of 0.79 falls in the UNEP humid class. Its basin is warmer than 10 of the 12 basins around it.

sections.title: Water
sections.text: No other basin drains into this one: its rivers rise within it. Lakes cover about 0.6% of the basin. The basin drains to the sea about 710 km beyond its outlet.

sections.title: Land and geology
sections.text: Across the basin, the land is very gently sloping on average (a mean slope of 1.9%), with topsoil that averages 43% sand, 39% silt and 18% clay (USDA texture class: loam). The underlying rock is mostly carbonate sedimentary rocks.

sections.title: Land cover around 2000
sections.text: Around 2000, about 44% of the basin is cropland and 13% is pasture; in the GLC2000 land cover map, the commonest class other than cultivated land is tree cover, mixed leaf type, at about 9%. Compared with the 12 basins around it, its basin has more cropland than 8 and less forest than 7.

sections.title: Surroundings
sections.text: Lviv's basin is one of 13 that meet here. None of them drains into it. It drains into one of them.

sections.title: About these figures
sections.text: The elevation and ecoregion under Setting are for Lviv itself. The other figures describe the basin of about 16,336 km² that contains it, from global datasets. Elevation and distances are measured from the place's point in WHG, which may be the centre of a town rather than its shore or riverbank.
